mainTopic: מילה overriding other laws: a בהרת, יום טוב, and preparations on שבת
overview: The גמרא shows that permitting מילה over a בהרת is a dispute between תנאים: רבי יאשיה learns it from the word 'בשר', and רבי יונתן learns it from a קל וחומר from שבת. The גמרא asks why any source is needed, since removing the בהרת is a דבר שאין מתכוין. אביי says the source is needed according to רבי יהודה, and רבא says it is needed even according to רבי שמעון, because this is a פסיק רישיה. Another version places this same discussion on a ברייתא about a rope or pole that indirectly rubs away צרעת. Under אביי's first view, רב עמרם and רב משרשיא explain that ״בשר״ covers a case where the person doing the מילה, even the father when no one else is available, intends to cut the spot. The גמרא then brings four sources for why a late מילה does not override יום טוב, from חזקיה, אביי, רבא, and רב אשי. רב rules like רבי עקיבא that preparations which could have been done before שבת do not override it, and the גמרא explains why this ruling was needed for both מילה and פסח. A new משנה then lists what may be done for a מילה on שבת, and what must be done in an unusual way if it was not prepared beforehand.

steps.title: The source is a dispute between תנאים: רבי יאשיה learns it from 'בשר'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the source for doing מילה over a בהרת is a dispute between תנאים. It quotes רבי יאשיה, who learns it from the word 'בשר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a dispute between תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: 'Flesh' means that even if there is a bright leprous spot there, he should circumcise. These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that two תנאים give different sources for the same law. It starts with רבי יאשיה, who says the word 'בשר' in the פסוק of מילה teaches that you circumcise even when a בהרת is on the foreskin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally it is forbidden to cut off a sign of צרעת. רבי יאשיה reads the extra word 'בשר' as a hint: cut the flesh no matter what is on it, even a בהרת. So מילה pushes aside the איסור of cutting off צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between Tannaim
As it was taught in a ברייתא
A bright white spot, one of the signs of צרעת
He should circumcise

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן agree on the law: you circumcise over a בהרת. They only disagree about where we learn it from.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim,
as it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: ״בָּשָׂר״ וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם בַּהֶרֶת —
phrases.english: 'Flesh': even though there is a bright white spot there,
phrases.notes: The word 'בשר' in the verse of מילה is read as including this case.

phrases.english: 'he shall circumcise'; these are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) about the source that מילה overrides צרעת. It shows that the source is a tannaitic dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יאשיה, the word 'בשר' teaches that one circumcises even over a בהרת.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: no פסוק is needed, since a קל וחומר from שבת works
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says we do not need the word 'בשר'. If מילה pushes aside the strict laws of שבת, it surely pushes aside צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: There is no need for this verse. If circumcision overrides שבת, which is stringent, then all the more so it overrides leprosy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן gives a different source for the same law. He uses logic, a קל וחומר, instead of a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת is a very strict איסור, punishable by סקילה, yet מילה on the eighth day still pushes it aside. The איסור of cutting off צרעת is lighter. So logically, מילה should push it aside too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed
Stringent, severe
Overrides, pushes aside
All the more so (the conclusion of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan says: It is not needed;
if circumcision overrides Shabbat, which is stringent,
then leprosy, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source, based on logic, for the same law that רבי יאשיה learned from a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יונתן, מילה overrides צרעת by a קל וחומר from שבת.

steps.title: Why is a verse needed, if cutting the spot is unintended?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יאשיה again and asks why any source is needed at all. The person only means to circumcise, and an unintended result is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Flesh' means that even if there is a bright spot there, he should circumcise; these are the words of רבי יאשיה. Why do I need a verse for this? It is an unintended act, and an unintended act is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the words of the ברייתא so it can challenge them. It asks why a פסוק is needed, since cutting off the בהרת is not what the person intends to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מוהל wants to do מילה. He does not want to remove the צרעת. There is a known rule that a דבר שאין מתכוין, an unintended side effect, is permitted. If so, we should not need the word 'בשר' to permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (re-quoting an earlier teaching in order to discuss it)
Why do I need a verse for this?
An unintended act or side effect
Permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This brings the general laws of unintended actions into the sugya. Those rules apply across all of שבת and many other areas of הלכה.

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: ״בָּשָׂר״, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם בַּהֶרֶת —
phrases.english: 'Flesh': even though there is a bright white spot there,
'he shall circumcise'; the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.
Why do I need a verse for this?
It is an unintended act,
and an unintended act is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes רבי יאשיה from step 1 in order to challenge the need for his derivation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יאשיה's need for the word 'בשר'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing the בהרת is unintended. Unintended acts are permitted anyway, so the פסוק seems unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: the verse is needed according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the פסוק is needed according to רבי יהודה, who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is only needed according to רבי יהודה, who says that an unintended act is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. The rule that unintended acts are permitted belongs to רבי שמעון. רבי יהודה disagrees, so according to him we need a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 3 assumed that everyone permits a דבר שאין מתכוין. אביי points out that רבי יהודה forbids it. According to רבי יהודה, cutting the בהרת would be forbidden without a פסוק, so 'בשר' is needed to permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for
The תנא who forbids unintended acts
Forbidden

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is only needed according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who said an unintended act is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by limiting the פסוק to רבי יהודה's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific opinion (רבי יהודה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question assumed that everyone permits unintended acts.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהודה, unintended acts are forbidden, so the פסוק is needed.

steps.title: רבא: needed even for רבי שמעון, because this is a פסיק רישיה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the פסוק is needed even according to רבי שמעון. This case is a פסיק רישיה, where the result is certain, and רבי שמעון agrees that such a case is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say it follows רבי שמעון, because רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. Even רבי שמעון, who permits unintended acts, would need this פסוק here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits unintended acts only when the forbidden result might not happen. Here, cutting the foreskin will definitely remove the בהרת, just as cutting off an animal's head will definitely kill it. When the result is certain, even רבי שמעון forbids it, so a פסוק is needed to permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
The תנא who permits unintended acts
Agrees, concedes
'Cut off its head and will it not die?': a case where the forbidden result is certain

steps.confusionAlert: A פסיק רישיה is still unintended, since the person does not want the result. It is forbidden only because the result is certain. 'Unintended' and 'certain' are two separate questions.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that even רבי שמעון forbids a פסיק רישיה is a major principle in הלכות שבת.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: Rava said: You can even say it follows Rabbi Shimon,
since Rabbi Shimon agrees
in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 3. It argues with אביי's need to limit the פסוק to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case as a פסיק רישיה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought this case is an ordinary unintended act, which רבי שמעון permits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The removal of the בהרת is certain, so even רבי שמעון would forbid it without a פסוק.

steps.title: Does אביי really reject the idea of פסיק רישיה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי did not answer like רבא. Elsewhere, אביי and רבא both say that רבי שמעון agrees in a case of פסיק רישיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does אביי not hold this reasoning? But אביי and רבא both said: רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי. If אביי himself accepts the rule of פסיק רישיה elsewhere, why did he limit the פסוק to רבי יהודה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer in step 4 implies that this is an ordinary unintended act. That suggests he does not apply the rule of פסיק רישיה. But a known statement quotes both אביי and רבא accepting that rule, which looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he not hold this reasoning?
But surely (introducing a contradiction)
Both of them

phrases.english: And does Abaye not hold this reasoning?
But Abaye and Rava both say:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּ״פְסִיק רֵישֵׁיהּ וְלָא יְמוּת״!
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer (step 4) using the principle רבא just stated (step 5).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי is quoted elsewhere accepting the rule of פסיק רישיה, so he should have answered like רבא.

steps.title: אביי accepted the idea only after hearing it from רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אביי first held his own view. Only after hearing רבא's reasoning did he agree to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he heard it from רבא, he accepted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by timing. אביי's answer here came first. His agreement to the rule of פסיק רישיה came later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two statements are not contradictory. They come from different stages. אביי changed his mind after hearing רבא's reasoning, and that is why he is later quoted together with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: After he heard it
He accepted it, agreed with it

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: אביי says the פסוק is needed for רבי יהודה. רבא says it is needed even for רבי שמעון, because this is a פסיק רישיה. אביי later agreed with רבא's principle.

phrases.english: After he heard it from Rava, he accepted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought אביי always held the rule of פסיק רישיה.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי accepted it only later, after hearing רבא.

steps.title: Another version places the אביי–רבא debate on a different ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some teach the אביי and רבא discussion on a different ברייתא. The פסוק forbids directly removing צרעת but permits actions that remove it indirectly, like wearing a rope on the foot or carrying a pole on the shoulder.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this discussion of אביי and רבא on the following: 'Take heed with the plague of leprosy, to observe diligently and to do.' Removing it directly you may not do. But you may wear a thick rope on your foot or carry a pole on your shoulder, and if the spot goes away, it goes away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up an alternate version of the אביי–רבא discussion. It first quotes the ברייתא that version is based on. The discussion itself follows in steps 9–13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids directly removing צרעת. It permits normal activities, like a rope rubbing the foot or a pole pressing on the shoulder, even if they happen to wear the spot away. This raises the same question about unintended acts, so some placed אביי's and רבא's answers here.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach (introducing an alternate version)
Take heed with the plague of צרעת (דברים כד:ח)
A thick rope
A pole or rod
And if it went away, it went away (no harm done)

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לְהָא דְּאַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא אַהָא:
phrases.english: Some teach this statement of Abaye and Rava on this:
'Take heed with regard to the plague of leprosy
to observe diligently and to do';
direct action to remove it you may not do,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עוֹשֶׂה אַתָּה בְּסִיב שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי רַגְלוֹ,
phrases.english: but you may wear a thick rope on his foot,
and a pole on his shoulder,
and if the spot went away, it went away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לְהָא דְּאַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an alternate version that moves the אביי–רבא discussion (steps 4–5) onto a different ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Directly removing צרעת is forbidden. Activities that might remove it indirectly are permitted.

steps.title: Why is a verse needed if the act is unintentional?
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, the גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs a פסוק to permit indirect actions like the rope or the pole. Removing the spot that way is a דבר שאין מתכוין, which is allowed anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a verse for this? It is an unintended act, and an unintended act is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is now working on the alternate ברייתא from Step 8. It asks the same kind of question as before: why does the תורה need a פסוק to allow the rope or pole, if removing the בהרת is unintended?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person wearing the rope or carrying the pole is not trying to remove the spot. According to רבי שמעון, an unintended result is permitted, so learning from ״ולעשות״ that such acts are allowed looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: An act whose forbidden result the person did not intend
A verse
Why do I need it?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a mistaken copy of the earlier steps. The גמרא is deliberately repeating the discussion because some teach it on a different ברייתא (Step 8).

phrases.english: But why do I need a verse?
It is an unintended act,
and an unintended act is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the פסוק in the alternate ברייתא from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's derivation from ״ולעשות״ that removing צרעת indirectly is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a דבר שאין מתכוין is allowed anyway, there is no reason for a פסוק to permit it.

steps.title: אביי: the verse is needed for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the פסוק is needed according to רבי יהודה, who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The verse is only needed according to רבי יהודה, who says that an unintended act is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from Step 9. He says the פסוק is written for the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids even acts a person did not intend. Under his view, wearing the rope or carrying the pole when it may wear away the בהרת would be forbidden without a פסוק, so the פסוק is needed to permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for...
The תנא who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין
Forbidden

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is only needed according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: an unintended act is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the פסוק to one תנא's view
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is needed according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבא: even רבי שמעון needs the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the פסוק is needed even according to רבי שמעון, because this case is a פסיק רישיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say it follows רבי שמעון, because רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. He says the פסוק is needed even according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the forbidden result is certain to happen (פסיק רישיה), even רבי שמעון forbids the act. Here the rope or pole will certainly wear away the בהרת, so a פסוק is needed to permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Cut off its head and it won't die?' A case where the forbidden result is certain
Agrees
You can even say

steps.whyThisMatters: פסיק רישיה is a basic rule of הלכות שבת and of other areas of הלכה: if the result is certain, a lack of intention does not help.

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: And Rava said: you can even say it follows Rabbi Shimon,
Rabbi Shimon agrees
in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 9 that works even for רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case as a פסיק רישיה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון would allow this act without any פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a פסיק רישיה, so even רבי שמעון needs the פסוק.

steps.title: Doesn't אביי also accept the certain-result rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי did not answer like רבא, since elsewhere both of them say that רבי שמעון agrees in a case of פסיק רישיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does אביי not accept this reasoning? But אביי and רבא both say that רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי. Elsewhere he says the same thing as רבא, so why did he need to bring in רבי יהודה here?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known statement in which both אביי and רבא say that רבי שמעון forbids a פסיק רישיה. If אביי holds that, he could have answered like רבא, which makes his answer look strange.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold this reasoning
Both of them

phrases.english: And does Abaye not accept this reasoning?
But Abaye and Rava both say:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּ״פְסִיק רֵישֵׁיהּ וְלָא יְמוּת״!
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer from Step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי elsewhere agrees with the פסיק רישיה rule, so his answer here seems inconsistent.

steps.title: אביי agreed only after hearing רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אביי accepted the rule only after he heard it from רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he heard it from רבא, he accepted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the contradiction by timing. אביי's answer here came first, and he changed his mind later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first אביי held that רבי שמעון allows even a certain result. Only after hearing רבא's reasoning did he agree. So there is no contradiction, just an earlier view and a later view.

keyTerms.meaning: After he heard it
He accepted it

phrases.english: After he heard it from Rava, he accepted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי first held his own view and later accepted רבא's reasoning.

steps.title: What does אביי learn from the word 'flesh'?
steps.stepSummary: Under אביי's original view of רבי שמעון, cutting the בהרת is permitted anyway, so the גמרא asks what the word ״בשר״ teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי's view of רבי שמעון, what does he do with this word 'flesh'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. If רבי שמעון allows the act even without a פסוק, the word ״בשר״ seems to have no purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה should teach something. Under אביי's first view, רבי שמעון does not need ״בשר״ to permit cutting the צרעת, so the גמרא wants to know what it does teach.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
'Flesh', the word in the פסוק about מילה
What does he do with it? (What does he learn from it?)

phrases.english: And Abaye, according to Rabbi Shimon,
what does he do with this word 'flesh'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּיֵי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַאי בְּשַׂר מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on אביי's original view and asks what the extra word teaches under it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word ״בשר״ under אביי's original view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the act is allowed without a פסוק, the word seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רב עמרם: it covers someone who intends to cut the spot
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם says ״בשר״ teaches that מילה overrides even when the person openly intends to cut off the בהרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: It refers to someone who says that he intends to cut off his bright spot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם answers Step 14. He gives the word ״בשר״ a new case to cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the person really does intend to remove the צרעת, it is no longer a דבר שאין מתכוין, so even רבי שמעון would forbid it. The פסוק teaches that מילה is still done and it overrides the איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: A bright white spot, a sign of צרעת
To cut off
Intends

phrases.english: Rav Amram said:
In a case where he says he intends to cut off his bright spot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 by finding a case for ״בשר״.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a new case for the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״בשר״ seemed to have no purpose for רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״בשר״ permits מילה even when the person intends to cut the בהרת.

steps.title: What about a baby, who has no intention?
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם's answer works for an adult. But a baby has no intention, so how does ״בשר״ apply to him?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for an adult. What is there to say about a minor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב עמרם's answer. It fits an adult giving himself מילה, but not a baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most מילה is done on babies, and a baby cannot intend anything. So רב עמרם's case of intention seems not to apply to an ordinary בריס.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well
An adult
A minor child
What is there to say?

phrases.english: This works well for an adult;
for a minor, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח גָּדוֹל קָטָן מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב עמרם's case from Step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A baby cannot intend, so the case does not apply to the most common מילה.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: the father has the intention
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא says the case is where the father, who does the מילה, intends to cut off his son's בהרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: It is where the father of the child says that he intends to cut off his son's bright spot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא answers Step 16. The intention belongs to the person doing the מילה, the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby does not need to intend anything. The father performs the מילה, and if he intends to remove the צרעת, the פסוק teaches that the מילה still overrides the איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: The father of the boy
Of his son

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
In a case where the father of the child says

phrases.aramaic: לָקוֹץ בַּהֶרֶת דִּבְנוֹ הוּא קָא מִתְכַּוֵּין.
phrases.english: that he intends to cut off his son's bright spot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by moving the intention to the father.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts the intention to the person doing the act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case of intention cannot apply to a baby.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father who does the מילה is the one with the intention.

steps.title: Let someone else do the circumcision
steps.stepSummary: If another person is available, he should do the מילה without intending to cut the צרעת. This follows ריש לקיש's rule that if you can keep both the עשה and the לא תעשה, you should.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if there is another person, let the other person do it! As רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: Wherever you find a positive מצוה and a negative מצוה, if you can keep both, that is best. If not, the positive מצוה comes and overrides the negative מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב משרשיא. Why should the father, who has a forbidden intention, do the מילה when someone else could do it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש teaches that a עשה only pushes aside a לא תעשה when there is no way to keep both. Here another person could do the מילה without intending to remove the צרעת, so both מצוות are kept and no override should be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Another person
A positive commandment
A negative commandment (a prohibition)
The positive commandment overrides the prohibition
It is best

steps.whyThisMatters: ריש לקיש's rule shows that עשה דוחה לא תעשה is a last resort. You must first try to keep both.

phrases.english: And if there is another person, let the other person do it!
As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה —
phrases.english: Any place you find a positive and a negative commandment,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְקַיֵּים שְׁנֵיהֶם מוּטָב,
phrases.english: if you can fulfill both, that is best;
and if not,
the positive commandment comes and overrides the negative one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב משרשיא's case from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב משרשיא's case of the father's intention
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under ריש לקיש's rule, if someone else can do the מילה without the forbidden intention, there is no need for the עשה to override the לא תעשה.

steps.title: There is no one else available
steps.stepSummary: The case is where no other person can do the מילה, so the father must do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where there is no other person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 18 and closes this discussion. Only the father is available to do the מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no one else can do the מילה, it is impossible to keep both commandments. So the עשה of מילה overrides the איסור of cutting צרעת, and ״בשר״ teaches that this is allowed even with the father's intention.

keyTerms.meaning: There is not

steps.whatToRemember: Under אביי's original view, ״בשר״ teaches that מילה overrides the איסור of cutting צרעת even when the person doing it intends to cut the spot. For a baby, this is where the father intends it and no one else is available to do the מילה.

phrases.english: It is where there is no other person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Another person could do the מילה and avoid the איסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: No one else is available, so the עשה overrides the לא תעשה.

steps.title: Asking for the source that late circumcision does not override a Festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ruling that מילה overrides יום טוב only on its proper day, and asks where this comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: circumcision overrides a Festival only at its proper time. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a ruling quoted earlier, that מילה overrides יום טוב only when done on the eighth day. It asks for the Torah source, which sets up the four answers that follow (steps 21–24).
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know from the previous steps that מילה is strong enough to override other laws. So why can't a late מילה override יום טוב? The גמרא wants a פסוק that limits it to its proper day.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said". This introduces a quote from a teaching cited earlier.
A Festival day, on which most מלאכה is forbidden
At its proper time (for מילה, the eighth day)
"From where do we know these things?" A request for a source.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about whether מילה is a מצוה. Everyone agrees it is. The question is only whether a late מילה is allowed to push aside the rules of יום טוב.

phrases.english: The Master said:
it (circumcision) does not override a Festival
phrases.notes: The subject is מילה. The ruling comes from the ברייתא quoted earlier.

phrases.english: except at its proper time alone.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about the בהרת and goes back to an earlier quoted ruling to ask for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that מילה שלא בזמנה does not override יום טוב.

steps.title: חזקיה's source: leftover פסח meat is burned on the second morning
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה learns from the extra words ״עד בקר״ that leftover קרבן פסח meat is burned on the second morning, not on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said, and the school of חזקיה taught the same: The verse says, "Do not leave any of it until morning." The תורה did not need to repeat "until morning." So why does it say "until morning"? The verse comes to give him a second morning for burning it.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers from the פסוק about leftover meat of the קרבן פסח. The extra words "until morning" teach that the leftovers are burned on the second morning, not on the first morning, which is יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning נותר is a מצוה, but it can wait, so it does not push aside יום טוב. In the same way, a late מילה is a מצוה that is not tied to this specific day, so it also may not override יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the study hall of חזקיה
"The verse says". This introduces a Torah source.
"The verse needed to say". Used to point out extra words in a פסוק.
Leftover sacrificial meat that must be burned
Burning

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main idea of the whole section: a מצוה that can be postponed does not override יום טוב.

phrases.english: Chizkiya said,
and so too the school of Chizkiya taught:
The verse says:
"You shall not leave any of it until morning"
phrases.notes: שמות יב:י. The פסוק continues: "and what remains of it until morning, burn in fire."

phrases.english: for the verse did not need to say "until morning" (again).
phrases.notes: "Until morning" appears twice in the פסוק, so the second time seems extra.

phrases.english: So why does it say "until morning"?
The verse comes to give him
a second morning for burning it.
phrases.notes: The first morning is the 15th of ניסן, which is יום טוב. The burning waits until the 16th.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה, וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מצוה that is not tied to the day, like burning נותר, does not override יום טוב. The same applies to מילה שלא בזמנה.

steps.title: אביי's source: only the day's own offerings are brought
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from ״עולת שבת בשבתו״ that a weekday עולה may not be brought on שבת or יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The verse says, "The burnt offering of שבת on its שבת". It is not the burnt offering of a weekday on שבת, and not the burnt offering of a weekday on a Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a different source. The פסוק teaches that only the offering that belongs to that day may be brought, not an offering from a regular day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even עבודה in the בית המקדש overrides שבת and יום טוב only when it is the required service of that day. In the same way, מילה overrides יום טוב only when the eighth day falls on that day. A late מילה is like a weekday offering.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering
The extra burnt offering required on שבת
A regular weekday

phrases.english: Abaye said: The verse says:
"The burnt offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat"
and not the burnt offering of a weekday on Shabbat,
and not the burnt offering of a weekday on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the same question from step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only what is required on that specific day overrides שבת or יום טוב. A late מילה is not required on that specific day.

steps.title: רבא's source: "that alone" excludes late circumcision
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from ״הוא לבדו״ that only food preparation is allowed on יום טוב. This excludes preparations for cooking (מכשירין) and late מילה, which we might otherwise have permitted by a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The verse says, "That alone may be done for you." "That" teaches: but not things that prepare for food-making. "Alone" teaches: but not circumcision that is not at its time, which we would otherwise have learned through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third source, from the פסוק that allows food preparation on יום טוב. The word ״לבדו״ ("alone") shuts out a late מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this word, we might reason with a קל וחומר: if making food, which is not even a מצוה, is allowed on יום טוב, then מילה, which is a מצוה, should surely be allowed. ״לבדו״ blocks that reasoning, so only food preparation is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Preparations for food-making, like fixing a cooking tool, as opposed to the cooking itself
"Alone" or "only". The word used here to exclude
An "all the more so" argument
Food preparation, which is permitted on יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: Three sources so far, one rule. Whether from נותר (חזקיה), from עולת שבת (אביי), or from ״לבדו״ (רבא), מילה overrides יום טוב only on the eighth day. A late מילה must wait. The next step adds a fourth source from רב אשי.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "דאתיא מקל וחומר" does not mean the קל וחומר is correct. It explains why ״לבדו״ was needed: to cancel a קל וחומר that would have permitted the late מילה.

phrases.english: Rava said: The verse says:
"That alone may be done for you"
phrases.notes: שמות יב:טז, said about food preparation on יום טוב.

phrases.english: "That": but not preparations for food-making.
"Alone": but not circumcision that is not at its time,
which would have come through a קל וחומר.
phrases.notes: If food preparation, which is not a מצוה, is permitted, then all the more so a מצוה like מילה should be. The word ״לבדו״ excludes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, independent answer to the question from step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לבדו״ limits the permitted work on יום טוב to food preparation, which excludes מילה שלא בזמנה even though a קל וחומר might have allowed it.

steps.title: רב אשי: יום טוב has both a positive and a negative מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a fourth answer. The Torah calls יום טוב a ״שבתון״, which is a positive commandment (עשה). So יום טוב has both an עשה and a לא תעשה, and the עשה of a late מילה cannot override both together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The word 'שבתון' is a positive commandment. So יום טוב has both a positive commandment and a negative commandment. A positive commandment does not push aside a negative commandment together with a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his own answer to the question from step 20: why does מילה override יום טוב only on its proper eighth day, and not when it is done late?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is עשה דוחה לא תעשה: a positive מצוה can push aside a negative one. רב אשי says that rule does not help here. יום טוב has a לא תעשה (do not do work) and also an עשה (״שבתון״, rest). A late מילה is only an עשה, and it is too weak to override an עשה and a לא תעשה together. Unlike the earlier answers, רב אשי does not need an extra word in a פסוק. He uses a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A day of rest.' The תורה's word for יום טוב, which רב אשי reads as a positive command to rest
A positive commandment, something you must do
A negative commandment, something you must not do

keyTerms.term: אֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה
keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה cannot override a negative מצוה and a positive מצוה together

steps.whatToRemember: There are four sources for why a late מילה does not override יום טוב: חזקיה (״עד בקר״), אביי (״עולת שבת בשבתו״), רבא (״הוא לבדו״), and רב אשי (״שבתון״ makes יום טוב both an עשה and a לא תעשה).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב אשי rejects the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה. He agrees with it. He is saying that the rule only works against a plain לא תעשה. It does not work against a לא תעשה that comes together with an עשה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
'Shabbaton' is a positive commandment,
phrases.notes: The Torah calls יום טוב a 'shabbaton,' a day of rest.

phrases.english: and so Yom Tov becomes
a positive commandment and a negative commandment,
and a positive commandment does not override
a negative commandment together with a positive commandment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a fourth answer to the question in step 20. It sits alongside the answers of חזקיה, אביי, and רבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יום טוב is both an עשה (״שבתון״) and a לא תעשה. A late מילה is only an עשה, so it cannot override both.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי עקיבא on preparations for מילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rule of רבי עקיבא from the משנה. Anything that could have been done before שבת does not override שבת. רב יהודה, quoting רב, says the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'רבי עקיבא stated a general rule, etc.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. That line is רבי עקיבא's general rule about preparations for מילה. It then records רב's ruling that the הלכה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's rule is this: any work that could have been done on ערב שבת, like preparing the knife, does not override שבת. Only work that cannot be done beforehand, the מילה itself, overrides שבת. רב makes this the practical הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
'Etc.' The quote from the משנה continues, but the גמרא shortens it
'The הלכה is like...' The practical ruling follows this opinion

phrases.english: 'Rabbi Akiva stated a general rule, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quoted from our משנה: whatever can be done before שבת does not override שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
The halacha follows Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts a new topic. The גמרא leaves the יום טוב discussion and turns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא: preparations for מילה that could have been done before שבת do not override שבת.

steps.title: The same rule and ruling for the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a similar משנה about קרבן פסח. There, רבי עקיבא gives the same rule: work that could be done before שבת does not override it, but the שחיטה itself, which cannot be done earlier, does. רב rules like רבי עקיבא there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned a similar משנה about the פסח offering. רבי עקיבא stated a general rule: any work that could be done on ערב שבת does not override שבת. The slaughtering, which cannot be done on ערב שבת, does override שבת. And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that רב gave the same ruling twice, once for מילה and once for פסח. This prepares the next step, where the גמרא will ask why both rulings were needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two משניות share the same logic. Only the core act, which has a fixed time, overrides שבת. Anything that could have been prepared earlier does not. Since the principle is identical, having two separate rulings from רב looks repetitive. That is what the next step will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And we also learned' in a משנה
'In a similar way,' a parallel case
Slaughtering, here of the קרבן פסח
The day before שבת

phrases.english: And we also learned regarding the Pesach offering
something similar to this:
Rabbi Akiva stated a general rule:
any work that is possible
to do on Erev Shabbat
does not override Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: The slaughtering, which cannot be done on Erev Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The Torah sets a fixed time for slaughtering the פסח, on the fourteenth of ניסן.

phrases.english: does override Shabbat.
And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
The halacha follows Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי פֶסַח כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This brings a parallel ruling. It quietly raises a question: why would רב need to say the same thing twice?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For פסח too, only the שחיטה overrides שבת, not preparations that could have been done earlier. The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Why the מילה ruling alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both rulings were needed. If רב had ruled only about מילה, we might think the rule is lenient there because delaying מילה carries no כרת. For פסח, where skipping it does carry כרת, we might have thought even the preparations override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both rulings are necessary. If רב had taught us only about מילה, we would say: it is there that preparations which could have been done the day before do not override שבת, because there is no כרת. But for פסח, where there is כרת, I might say the preparations should override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the hidden question of why רב repeated himself. It begins by showing what we would have wrongly assumed if we only had the מילה ruling. The other half, why the פסח ruling alone would not be enough, comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Failing to bring the קרבן פסח is punished with כרת, which makes פסח very serious. A father's delay of his son's מילה carries no כרת. So we might have reasoned that פסח is serious enough for even its preparations to override שבת. רב's separate ruling about פסח teaches that this is not so.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is necessary,' meaning both statements are needed and neither is extra
'He taught us'
From yesterday, meaning the day before
Spiritual cutting off, a severe punishment from Heaven
'I might say,' what we would mistakenly think

steps.confusionAlert: מילה does have כרת, but only for an adult who stays uncircumcised. The father's delay on the eighth day carries no כרת. That is why the גמרא says here that there is 'no כרת' for מילה.

phrases.english: And both are necessary,
for if he had taught us only about milah,
I would say it is there that the preparations
which could be done the day before
do not override Shabbat
because there is no karet,
but for Pesach, where there is karet,
I might say they should override Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the implied question from step 26 about why רב gave two rulings. It covers the first half of the צריכותא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each statement teaches something the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because skipping פסח carries כרת, its preparations might override שבת even though the preparations for מילה do not.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's separate ruling on פסח shows that even there, preparations that could be done before שבת do not override it.

steps.title: Why the פסח ruling alone would not have been enough
steps.stepSummary: If רב had ruled like רבי עקיבא only about פסח, we might have thought מילה is different. Thirteen covenants were made over מילה, so its preparations might override שבת. That is why both rulings were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if רב had taught us the rule only about the קרבן פסח, we would say: there it applies because thirteen covenants were not made over פסח. But מילה, over which thirteen covenants were made, we might say should override שבת even for its preparations. So both rulings were necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the second half of its 'both rulings were needed' answer. This time it shows why the פסח ruling could not teach us about מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 27, פסח looked stricter than מילה because skipping פסח carries כרת. Now מילה looks stricter in a different way: the Torah mentions ברית (covenant) thirteen times in connection with מילה. Since each case has its own special strength, neither ruling can be learned from the other, so רב had to state both.

keyTerms.meaning: Thirteen covenants: the word ברית appears 13 times in the Torah's section about אברהם's מילה
It is necessary: both statements were needed
I might have said
Let it override

steps.whatToRemember: Each case has its own strength: פסח has כרת and מילה has 13 covenants. Neither can be learned from the other, so רב ruled like רבי עקיבא in both. The final rule is that preparations which could have been done before שבת do not override שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the section on רבי עקיבא's rule and sets the practical הלכה. That rule is the background for the next משנה about what may be done for a מילה on שבת.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only regarding Pesach,
we would say it is because there were not made over it
thirteen covenants.
But circumcision, over which were made
thirteen covenants,
I would say it should override Shabbat (even for its preparations),
therefore it was necessary (to state both).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the צריכא begun in Step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each ruling is needed because each case has its own special strength
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because מילה has thirteen covenants, its preparations might override שבת
steps.terutzMaskana: Even for מילה, preparations that could be done before שבת do not override it, so both rulings were needed

steps.title: New משנה: all the needs of the circumcision itself are done on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that all the essential parts of a מילה are done on שבת. These are cutting, uncovering (פריעה), and sucking the blood. One may also put a bandage and cumin on the wound.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We do all the needs of a מילה on שבת. We cut, we uncover (the membrane), we suck the blood, and we put a bandage and cumin on the wound.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the actions that are fully allowed on שבת for a מילה that falls on the eighth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits רבי עקיבא's rule. These actions cannot be done before שבת, because they are the מילה itself and the immediate care of the wound right after it. So they override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The needs of the circumcision
Uncovering (פריעה): peeling back the thin membrane under the foreskin
Sucking (מציצה) the blood from the wound
A bandage or compress placed on the wound
Cumin, used as a healing salve

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
We perform all the needs of circumcision on Shabbat:
we circumcise, and uncover, and suck the blood,
and place on it a bandage and cumin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה in the same perek, applying the topic of מילה on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting, פריעה, מציצה, and applying a bandage and cumin are all permitted on שבת

steps.title: If the cumin was not ground or the wine and oil were not mixed before Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: If the cumin was not ground before שבת, one chews it with his teeth instead. If wine and oil were not mixed before שבת, each one is put on the wound separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not grind the cumin before שבת, he chews it with his teeth and puts it on. If he did not mix wine and oil before שבת, he puts this one on by itself and that one on by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with preparations that should have been done before שבת. It shows how to manage without doing them the normal way on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grinding and mixing could have been done before שבת, so following רבי עקיבא they may not be done the normal way on שבת. Instead, the משנה allows an unusual method: chewing instead of grinding, or applying each liquid separately instead of mixing. This way the baby still gets the treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: Ground (crushed into powder)
Chews with his teeth: an unusual way that is not real grinding
Mixed or beat together
From before שבת (ערב שבת)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה is allowing grinding on שבת. Chewing is allowed exactly because it is not the normal way of grinding. Grinding itself was supposed to be done before שבת.

phrases.english: If he did not grind (the cumin) before Shabbat,
he chews it with his teeth and places it.
If he did not mix wine and oil
before Shabbat,
he places this by itself and that by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from the מילה itself to preparations that could have been done earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Preparations skipped before שבת may be replaced only by an unusual method: chewing the cumin, and applying wine and oil separately

steps.title: No pouch may be made, but a rag may be wrapped and carried on the finger
steps.stepSummary: One may not make a fitted pouch for the wound on שבת, but one may wrap a rag around it. If the rag was not brought ahead of time, one wraps it on his finger and brings it, even from another courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not make a pouch for it at the outset, but he may wrap a rag over it. If he did not prepare it before שבת, he wraps it on his finger and brings it, even from a different courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with the bandage. It explains what kind of dressing may be used, and how to bring it if it was not set up before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a pouch would mean sewing or shaping a new item, so it is not allowed. Simply wrapping a rag is allowed. Carrying the rag could have been done before שבת, so it is allowed only in an unusual way: worn on the finger like clothing. This is permitted even from a courtyard where carrying would normally be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A pouch or fitted covering (literally 'a shirt') for the wound
At the outset, as the first choice
A rag
Prepared or set up in advance
A different courtyard, where carrying would normally be forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern of this משנה: the מילה itself and its immediate care override שבת. Anything that could have been prepared before שבת is allowed only with a change (שינוי): chewing, applying separately, or wrapping on the finger.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical application of רבי עקיבא's rule, which the previous section just ruled is the הלכה.

phrases.english: And we do not make a pouch for it at the outset,
but he may wrap a rag over it.
If he did not prepare it before Shabbat,
he wraps it on his finger and brings it,
and even from a different courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with rules about the bandage
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No new pouch may be made, but a rag may be wrapped. If it was not brought before שבת, it is carried wrapped on the finger, even from another courtyard.
